question: The value of 2 - sqrt {frac{{cot theta + cos theta }}{{cot theta - cos theta }}} , when 0° θ is equal to:
solution:
**Formula used:**

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ

cot θ = 1 / tan θ 

cos² θ = 1 - sin2 θ

**Calculations:**

Substituting cot θ for 1over tan θ-

⇒ 2 - sqrt{{1over tan θ}+cos θ over{1over tan θ} -cos θ}

⇒ 2 - sqrt{ 1+sin θ over 1 - sin θ}

Rationalizing sqrt{ 1+sin θ over 1 - sin θ}, we get-

⇒ 2 - sqrt{ (1+sin θ)² over (1-sin²θ}

⇒ 2 - [1+ sin θ] over cosθ

⇒ 2 - 1over cos θ - tan θ

⇒ 2 - sec θ - tan θ

**The answer to the expression is 2 - sec θ - tan θ.**
